AI systems for owner-led businesses

More gets done.

Less lands on you.

Bob is your AI teammate. Together, we connect your tools and build software that helps your team see what’s happening and get work done.

See Bob at WorkTalk About Your Business

Built around your business. Backed by the Buildwise team.

Meet Bob

A familiar face. A useful teammate.

Give Bob one clear job. We connect the facts and tools, set the limits, and check the work. The Buildwise team stays responsible.

Keep leads moving.

Give each inquiry a clear next step.

Keep service work connected.

Put the case, owner, and promised update in one place.

Catch gaps before a handoff.

Bring open questions to a person who can make the call.

Seven ways to put AI to work. Follow the examples below, or start with a clearer view of your business →

2 of 7 · Service management

Catch gaps before they

reach the customer.

We designed a service system that keeps the case, owner, and customer update together. Bob checks the record and flags gaps for your team to review.

The gapA note claims more than the record supports.

Bob’s partFlag the mismatch and propose a next step.

The person’s partCheck the evidence before sending the update.

3 of 7 · Connected business data

One business.

One clearer picture.

Sales in one tool. Jobs in another. Money in a third. We bring the records you choose into a shared view, so you can see how the work connects and where it needs attention.

Sales

Marketing

Jobs

Customers

Money

Connect the records. See the links. Keep the missing facts in view.

Illustrated use cases · Sample records

Ask a better business question.

Which finished jobs still need an invoice?

Job: completeInvoice: draft

Check the invoice before closing the job.

Which sources bring us good leads?

Inquiry: bookedSource: missing

See which links are known and which still need a fact.

Did the job cost what we planned?

Quote: on fileFinal cost: missing

Get the missing cost before calling it profitable.

We build connected reports for our own team and for clients. Your tools stay the source of the facts. Which records connect depends on the tools you use. We agree on that and the questions to answer before work starts.

Connect Your Business Data

4 of 7 · Your website

One website.

Three kinds of visitor.

A customer may visit your site, ask an AI to research you, or use a service that needs your business details. We build for all three, with clear facts and a useful next step.

Your website.

The same clear facts.

Services · Areas · Hours · Contact · Proof

Human to human

A person finds your team.

Example visit

They find the right service, see your work and talk to a person.

AI to human

Their AI finds useful facts.

Example research

Their assistant reads your services, area and contact details to help them choose.

AI to AI

A request reaches your team.

Possible connection

One system passes a request to another. Your team checks it before a booking is confirmed.

Clear pages and facts that machines can read are part of our website builds. System handoffs are built for each project. Search and AI tools decide what they show; no ranking or mention is promised.

5 of 7 · Meeting follow-up

Turn the call into the next step.

Bob pulls tasks, owners and decisions from a recorded call, with the words that support them. Your team checks the list and clears up anything that is still unclear.

Sample meeting note

“I’ll check the revised quote before Friday.”

Alex, on the callCheck revised quoteOwner: Alex · Due: before FridayReady for the team to check

Built for our own team. A call alone does not send a customer message.

One set of facts.

More ways to use it.

A spec sheet and photos become a shared fact record, then a page, posts and a flyer. The same source supports each draft. Your team reviews before anything is published.

7 of 7 · Company knowledge

Find the answer.

Keep the source.

We can build a question-and-answer tool around your approved documents. Answers show their sources. Staff see the material they are allowed to use. Gaps go to your team for review.

Talk About Your First Job

The seven examples above are starting points. You can describe any of them in your note.

How we start

One clear job.

A 90-day Pilot.

One agreed job.

A system your team can use.

Start with the job that matters most: a better follow-up, a clearer business view, or another use for the facts you already have. Before work starts, we agree on the scope, the checks, and what your team needs to use the system.

1

Build the agreed system.

A defined job, with clear limits.

2

Check the work together.

Review the result against the agreed checks.

3

Choose the next step.

Review the handoff and any continuing work.

Scope, fees, ownership, access and support are set in the written agreement. The 90 days describe the first engagement, not a guaranteed result or completion date.
